# Court Vision: full guide text

Source: https://courtvisiongame.com/ (updated 2026-11-12). Court Vision is a free browser basketball GM and simulation game.

---

# About Court Vision

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/about.html

CourtVision is a free browser basketball management and simulation game developed by NineFoldVision. Its focus is letting you explore basketball decisions: build a roster, change a rotation, replay a historical matchup or follow a player’s career, then see how those choices play out possession by possession.

## What you can do

- **Run a franchise (GM mode).** Draft, trade, negotiate contracts with agents, hire coaches, handle injuries, set rotations and play through the regular season, the In-Season Cup, the trade deadline, the playoffs and the offseason. See [How to Play](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html).
- **Play real NBA history.** Start a league in any season from 1946-47 to today with real players, real rosters and their real careers, awards and champions. See [Real NBA history](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/real-nba-history.html).
- **League Hunt.** Spin a six-man squad from all of basketball history and win ten best-of-seven series against the great teams of every era. See the [League Hunt guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/league-hunt.html).
- **Career Mode.** Create one player and live his entire career, from draft night to the Hall of Fame and the all-time Top 100. See the [Career Mode guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/career-mode.html).
- **Rebuild Challenge.** Take over a real team at its lowest point and win a title before time runs out. See the [Rebuild Challenge guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/rebuild-challenge.html).
- **82-0 Challenge.** Spin or pick a ten-man team from all of history and try to go 82-0, then 16-0 in the playoffs, against real teams and boss teams like the 72-10 Bulls. See the [82-0 Challenge guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/82-0-challenge.html).
- **All-Time Draft.** Thirty teams, thirteen rounds, every player in history at his best: draft against AI GMs, then play the season. See the [All-Time Draft guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/all-time-draft.html).
- **Survival.** Keep a team competitive while defeated opponents claim players from your roster. Protect your Franchise Player and decide when to spend shields.
- **Story Mode.** Follow Street to the League through basketball games, characters and decisions.
- **Your Career.** Begin at age 13 and choose a route through youth basketball and professional opportunities. Compare all seven main modes in the [FAQ](https://courtvisiongame.com/faq.html).

## How the simulation works

Every game is simulated play by play. Players have more than seventy ratings (shooting from every zone, finishing, passing, defense, rebounding, athleticism, basketball IQ and more) and tendencies that decide what they try to do. Coaches set pace, three-point frequency, defensive schemes and rotations. The engine is calibrated against real NBA league averages for pace, shooting, fouls and assists, so box scores look like real box scores.

You can watch any game on a pixel-art court, coach it live from the sideline (timeouts, play calls, double teams, last-shot plays), or simulate whole seasons in seconds. Simulation runs in background workers, so the game stays responsive while a season plays out.

## Your saves stay with you

Local leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds stay in your browser. An optional account syncs supported profile progress and retired Career Mode records; it is not a full league backup. Download a backup from the GM Locker or Backups before moving devices or clearing browser data. The [FAQ](https://courtvisiongame.com/faq.html) explains recovery, and the [Privacy Policy](https://courtvisiongame.com/privacy.html) describes storage and advertising.

You can also install Court Vision as an app on your PC or phone: it gets its own icon and window and plays offline. Open [courtvisiongame.com/#/install](https://courtvisiongame.com/./#/install) for the steps.

## Data and credits

The built-in NBA history (statistics, awards and drafts) comes from [Basketball-Reference.com](https://www.basketball-reference.com/), compiled by Sumitro Datta in the [bball-reference-datasets](https://github.com/sumitrodatta/bball-reference-datasets) project. Champions, Finals MVPs, All-Star Game MVPs and Coaches of the Year come from [NBA.com](https://www.nba.com/news/history-all-time-awards). Player ratings, skill attributes and team names are Court Vision's own, computed from the statistics.

Court Vision is an independent fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the NBA, its teams, its players or these data sources.

## Community

Share your leagues and careers, report bugs and suggest features on our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/5uGK5HDS8e). New features ship regularly; see the [changelog](https://courtvisiongame.com/changelog.html).

---

# How to Play

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html

This guide walks you through your first season as general manager, from picking a team to your first offseason. Everything here applies to both random leagues and real NBA history leagues.

## 1. Start a league

1. On the main menu, choose **Franchise**, then select a generated league, a real historical league or one of the available challenge setups.
2. Pick a trade difficulty. **Normal** means trades need roughly matched value; **Hard** puts a premium on young high-potential players.
3. Choose a team to run, or create an expansion team through a real expansion draft where every club files a protection list first.
4. Pick **Simple** navigation for a guided sidebar, or **Full** to see every page. You can switch any time.

## 2. Set your rotation

Open **Roster** to order your depth chart: the first five are starters. Minutes targets decide who plays how much. Players who get fewer minutes than they expect lose morale and some ask to be traded, so give your best players the minutes they have earned.

Your head coach's system (pace, three-point frequency, defensive scheme) shapes how the team plays. The **Coaching** page lets you adjust tendencies; the coaching staff also affects player development.

## 3. Play the season

Use the **Play** button to simulate a day, a week, to the next event or the rest of the season. The season stops for the big moments:

- **In-Season Cup:** group games, a knockout bracket and a final you can watch.
- **All-Star Weekend:** captains draft their teams, plus the three-point contest, dunk contest and Rising Stars.
- **Trade Deadline Day:** a 9 AM to 3 PM clock, a rumor mill, AI teams calling with offers, and deals breaking all day.
- **Playoffs:** a play-in, four rounds, and your series live if you want to watch.

## 4. Make moves

- **Trades.** Build an offer and the AI front office answers, often with a counteroffer instead of a flat no. Three-team trades are possible too.
- **Free agency.** Players weigh money, role, winning and loyalty. Negotiate through their agents; a player who walks away will not sign with you that offseason.
- **Contracts.** Extend players during the season before they reach free agency. Watch the salary cap and the luxury tax on the Finances page.
- **Medical room.** When a player is hurt, the doctors ask for a call: rest him longer or bring him back early at a risk.

## 5. The offseason

After the Finals come the awards, the Draft Lottery and Draft Night, where you can trade picks in the war room. Summer League follows, then re-signings, then free agency. Players age and develop over the summer: young players with minutes and good coaching grow the most. Your owner reviews your season against the goals set before it, and your job security depends on it.

## Tips for your first season

- Check **Power Rankings** and **Standings** before trading: know whether you are a contender or a seller.
- A young player's **Potential** is his ceiling; minutes and coaching decide how close he gets.
- Use **Auto Play** to simulate several seasons at once when you want to see a rebuild through.
- Back up your progress now and then from the main menu (Backups) or the GM Locker.

## The All-Time Draft

Pick **All-Time Draft** on the main menu, choose your franchise, your draft slot (or a random one) and the era whose rules the season is played under. Thirty teams then draft in snake order for thirteen rounds from every player in NBA history, each at his best season. The table shows every player's rating, best season and, for the all-time greats, their place in the all-time Top 100; filter by guards, forwards or bigs, or search a name.

AI GMs take the best player left for what their roster still needs, so bigs and guards run out as the rounds go on. **Best fit** suggests your pick, and **Auto-draft the rest** finishes for you. When the draft is done you see where your team ranks on paper; then the season starts in a normal GM league: trades, free agency, the draft, and as many seasons as you like, with players aging and developing from their best years.

---

# Career Mode guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/career-mode.html

In Career Mode you create one player and live his whole career, season by season, in a real league played by the full simulation engine. At the end you see where he ranks among the greatest players of all time.

## Choose when he enters the league

Start in today's league (the 2026 draft) or pick any past draft from 1947 to 2025. In a past draft the league is real NBA history from the season before: real rosters, real players on their real careers, and the real draft class. Enter the 1984 draft and you share the stage with Michael Jordan, Hakeem Olajuwon and Charles Barkley.

## Random mode: the wheel

Every real player in NBA history sits on the wheel once, at his best season. The odds lean a little toward good players: a Star comes up about 7% of the time and a Great about 18%. When the wheel stops you take one of that player's ten categories, and your player gets his exact ratings in it.

| Category | What it copies |
| --- | --- |
| Height & Length | height, wingspan and standing reach |
| Body | weight, strength, balance, stamina and durability |
| Athleticism | speed, acceleration, vertical and agility |
| Finishing | layups, dunks, touch and the post |
| Mid-Range | mid-range, long twos and free throws |
| Three-Point | every kind of three |
| Playmaking | handles, passing and decisions |
| Perimeter D | on-ball defense, closeouts and steals |
| Interior D & Boards | rim protection, blocks and rebounding |
| IQ & Clutch | basketball IQ, clutch, composure and consistency |

Tools: **Move Left** and **Move Right** shift a stopped wheel by one slice (once each), two **Respins** spin again without taking anything, and one **Triple Spin** spins three wheels at once so you can take a category from each.

The best ever at a skill go past 99. The top 60 in each skill, ranked by what they actually did that season (threes made, assists, steals, rebounds and blocks, efficient scoring), carry up to +21, so the very best reach 120. Take Stephen Curry's shooting and your player shoots like the best shooter ever. On the court, points above 99 count half, so a 120 shooter is the greatest ever, not a 70% three-point shooter.

## MyPlayer: build him yourself

Set height, weight and wingspan, then spend a budget of points across nine skills. Height sets the limits: a seven-footer cannot handle like a point guard and a small guard cannot protect the rim like a center. You also choose how ready he is: a late bloomer starts further from his prime but peaks higher; an NBA-ready rookie starts close to it.

## Every season

- **Draft night.** Where he goes depends on his rating and potential against the rest of the class.
- **Training focus.** Each summer pick two categories. They grow faster, and training can carry them past his prime. Everything grows quickly when he is young and declines with age, athleticism first.
- **Free agency.** When his contract runs out he gets offers: the biggest contract, a title contender, the biggest role, or his old team.
- **Trade requests.** Ask out to a contender, for a bigger role, or anywhere but here.
- **Autopilot.** Let the game make sensible choices for the rest of his career; take control back whenever you like.

Each season shows his stats, his team's record and playoff run, every award, and the moments of his year: his first 40-point game, his first triple-double, 20,000 career points.

## Legacy, the Hall of Fame and the Top 100

When he retires you get his full career: totals, per-game averages, a pixel trophy shelf, his Overall by age, and any team that retires his number (five seasons there plus three All-Star years, a title or an MVP). His **Legacy Score** decides the Hall of Fame (45 gets him in, 90 makes him a first-ballot pick) and his place on the all-time Top 100. The [Ratings explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html) guide shows how the score is built.

Your Hall of Famers get plaques in the Career Mode Hall of Fame and in the GM Locker. A retired or active player can also be brought into any GM league from the Free Agency page.

## Big moments

After a season with something special in it (a title, an MVP, a 50-point night, a first All-Star selection, a playoff exit, the rookie wall, or the first signs of Father Time) you make a call. Every answer is worth something: **Legacy Score** right away, or a summer of extra work in one skill that shows up in your ratings next season. Your calls appear in the career timeline. On autopilot, seasons play on without them.

---

# League Hunt guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/league-hunt.html

League Hunt is a quick run through basketball history. Build a six-man squad and a coach from any era, then win ten best-of-seven series against real teams, each played under the rules of its time.

## The spins

The draft is a slot machine with seven reels: point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, center, sixth man (any position) and coach. They all spin at once; you hit STOP, lock one of the seven, and the rest spin again, until every slot is locked. Cards are player-seasons, so 1996 Michael Jordan and 2003 Michael Jordan are different cards. Early rounds are richer than late ones, and one early round always lands a Star on the reels, another a Great.

Coaches add from -2 to +5 overall to everyone and bring a style: defense, pace, threes or ball movement. A coach also adds a point of chemistry for players from a franchise he won with.

## Team rating, 0 to 100

Every team, yours included, has a rating from its best six players with the star weighted most. The scale follows real results: 60 is a bad team, 70 about 40 wins, 80 about 45, 90 a 55 to 62 win team, and 100 a 68-win all-time great. More in [Ratings explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html).

## The road

- Ten best-of-seven series against real teams, each played under its era's rules: no three-point line before 1979-80, hand-checking in the 1990s, the pace of the time.
- Series 5 is a semi-boss and series 10 is the boss, one of the best teams ever, rated 100.
- From series 2 on, teams bring buffs such as Superstar Takeover, Hostile Crowd or Playoff Veterans. Bosses bring more, and stronger ones.
- Losing a series costs a life, and you replay it.

## Boosts, the shop and your focus

After a series win you pick one of three boosts; a hunt holds three. Many grow inside a series: the Sixth Man Spark adds +3 to your sixth man for every game you have won in it. Boosts add at most +6 to one player in one game.

A shop comes before series 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9: players for a specific slot, a better coach, items that last the whole hunt, and training. Lives are for sale only on Rookie. You also pick what the team works on: developing the star, developing the sixth man, team chemistry, or the coach's system.

## Decks, difficulty and the Daily Legend

- **Decks** change how the draft opens: Big Man Era, Old School (pre-1980 players only), Pace & Space (2010 on) and Dynasty. They unlock as you play.
- **Difficulty:** Rookie (softer teams, four lives), Pro, and Legend (tougher teams, two lives, a top-four all-time boss).
- **Daily Legend:** one hunt a day, the same for everyone. Keep your streak going.
- **Album:** every card you have had on a squad, with progress toward each era's stars.
- **Dream Matchup:** play any two real team-seasons against each other under any era's rules.

---

# 82-0 Challenge guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/82-0-challenge.html

The 82-0 Challenge asks one question: can your team go undefeated? Build a ten-man team and a coach from all of NBA history, play a full 82-game season against real teams from every era, then four best-of-seven playoff rounds. The goal is 82-0, then 16-0.

## Two ways to build

- **Quick Spin:** ten spins (point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward and center, then five bench spots) and a coach spin. Whatever the reel lands on is yours. Fast and full of luck.
- **Franchise Spin:** each spin rolls a franchise and an era, for example the Warriors in the 2010s. You see everyone who played there in that era, each at his best season with the team, and pick **one**. You get one team reroll, one era reroll and one **Absolute Prime** boost, which shows that spin's players at the best season of their whole career. More choice, tougher opponents.
- **From League Hunt:** after you win a hunt, you can take that six-man squad and its coach into an 82-0 season, plus four bench spins. Hunt squads have their own record.

## The season and the bosses

The 82 games are against real team-seasons, getting tougher as the season goes on, and every game is played under the rules of the opponent's era. Six boss teams sit on the schedule: Wilt's 68-13 Sixers, the 1971-72 Lakers who won 33 straight, Bird's 1985-86 Celtics, the 72-10 Bulls, the 73-9 Warriors and the 2016-17 Warriors. The playoffs are four best-of-seven rounds against stronger and stronger teams, ending with a champion.

You can play one game at a time, or sim the season and watch the record tick up. A banner tracks whether 82-0 is still alive, and when the streak breaks it shows the game and the team that did it.

## Lineups and chemistry

- Your five best players start. If no guard starts, or no big man (center or power forward) starts, the starters play worse. Three starters at one position also costs a little.
- Real teammates from the same season, players from the same franchise and famous rivals on the same side play better together.
- Ratings are ranked within each season, so a 1965 star and a 2016 star stand on the same scale. See [Ratings explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html).

## Scoring

| What | Points |
| --- | --- |
| Each regular-season win | 100, plus the winning margin up to 25 |
| Each boss team beaten | 400 |
| Each playoff win | 200 |
| Each sweep | 250 |
| The title | 1,500 |
| Going 82-0 | 5,000 |
| Then 16-0 in the playoffs | 5,000 more |

## Daily 82-0, records and rewards

- **Daily 82-0:** the same spins for everyone each day, alternating between Quick Spin and Franchise Spin. Your best try of the day counts, and your best day of the week goes on the online weekly board.
- **Rewards:** the Undefeated title and profile frame for an 82-0 season, and the gold Perfection title and frame for 98-0 (82-0 and 16-0). Five achievements and Trophy Road points for your best season, titles and perfect seasons.
- **Share cards:** a landscape card or a 9:16 card for TikTok and Stories, with your whole season as a strip of wins and losses.

---

# All-Time Draft guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/all-time-draft.html

The All-Time Draft puts every player in NBA history into one draft pool, each at his best season. Thirty teams take turns for thirteen rounds; you draft against AI GMs, then play a full season with the whole GM game.

## How the draft works

- Thirty teams, thirteen rounds: a full roster for everyone.
- Every player in history is in the pool at his best season, so the first picks are the greatest players ever.
- AI GMs draft for need: a team with three guards goes looking for a big man. A draft board shows every pick, the clock, and the steals and reaches.

## The draft pool

Every player in the history data appears once, at his best season: the season with his highest rating, or on a tie his most productive one. The pool is ranked by draft value. That is the best-season rating plus a bonus for a place in the all-time Top 100 (from +1 for number 100 to +3.5 for number 1), with a small discount for seasons before 1965.

The bonus exists because many legends share the top rating, since each rating is measured against its own season. It is what makes Michael Jordan and LeBron James go before a 1950s scoring leader with the same number.

## Snake order

The order reverses every round, so the team that picks 30th in round one picks first in round two. Picking late in round one means two picks close together at the turn, a good moment to take a pair of players who fit together.

## How the AI GMs draft

- Each AI GM takes the best player left, adjusted for need. A roster aims for 4 to 6 guards, 4 to 6 forwards and 2 to 4 centers.
- Below the minimum at a position, a player there gets a small boost. When the picks left are only just enough to fill the holes, the boost becomes large and the GM fills the hole now.
- At the maximum at a position, players there are strongly marked down. You will rarely see an AI team take a seventh guard.
- Every GM also has a little taste of his own, so two teams with the same needs do not always take the same player.

| Difficulty | How the AI GMs draft |
| --- | --- |
| Rookie | Loosely, with more reaches |
| Pro | Mostly by the board |
| Legend | They barely miss |

Your own auto-pick always uses the standard logic, whatever the difficulty.

## The league after the draft

- The drafted rosters move into a full league with the base league's 30 franchises: their names, schedule, coaches and finances.
- Contracts are scaled so every payroll sits around the salary cap, so nobody starts with an impossible cap sheet.
- The next 60 best players who were not drafted become free agents.
- The league plays under one era's rules, from the 1960s with no three-point line and a fast pace to today's three-heavy game. Pick the era before you draft: a dominant center is worth more without a three-point line.
- There is no imported history in this league. From the opening tip, players age and develop through Court Vision's own systems, for one season or as long as you want.

## After the draft

Your drafted team plays a full season in the GM game, under the rules of the era you choose: trades, rotations, coaching, the playoffs. Titles count toward your GM legacy and achievements.

## All-Time Draft of the Week

Every week there is a shared All-Time Draft with the same order, era and AI GMs for everyone, so you can compare drafts with friends.

## Tips

- Take the best player available early, then fill positions: a team needs someone to bring the ball up and someone to protect the rim.
- Late rounds are where role players win titles: shooters and defenders matter more than names.
- Learn how player ratings compare across eras in [Ratings explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html).

---

# Rebuild Challenge guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/rebuild-challenge.html

Take over a real team at the lowest point in its history and win a championship before time runs out. The league is real NBA history from that season, and you run the team with every tool of the full game.

## The scenarios

| Scenario | Team and first season | Seasons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Life After Michael | Chicago, 1998-99 | 6 |
| Celtics in Ruins | Boston, 1996-97 | 6 |
| The Clipper Curse | LA Clippers, 1998-99 | 8 |
| Before the Dynasty | Golden State, 2000-01 | 8 |
| Wolves in the Wilderness | Minnesota, 2009-10 | 7 |
| The Decision, Undone | Cleveland, 2010-11 | 5 |
| After 7-59 | Charlotte, 2012-13 | 7 |
| Trust the Process | Philadelphia, 2013-14 | 6 |
| Garden of Despair | New York, 2014-15 | 6 |
| The Post-Kobe Lakers | LA Lakers, 2016-17 | 5 |
| The Longest Drought | Sacramento, 2016-17 | 7 |
| Motor City Reset | Detroit, 2020-21 | 5 |
| Eleven and Seventy-One | Dallas, 1993-94 | 7 |
| Mile-High Misery | Denver, 1998-99 | 6 |
| Wade Alone | Miami, 2008-09 | 5 |
| Up From 13-69 | Atlanta, 2005-06 | 6 |
| Orlando After T-Mac | Orlando, 2004-05 | 6 |
| Twelve and Seventy | New Jersey, 2010-11 | 6 |
| The Greek Freak Project | Milwaukee, 2014-15 | 6 |

## How it plays

You start with the real roster of that season. Around you, real players follow their real careers and real draft classes arrive each year, so the 2003 class still holds LeBron James and the 1984 class Michael Jordan, but where they land depends on the lottery and on you. Trades, free agency, the draft and coaching all work as in the main game.

## Rebuild of the Week

Every Monday at 00:00 UTC a new Rebuild of the Week starts on the main menu. It picks one scenario and one twist, and builds the league from a seed shared by everyone, so every player starts from the same rosters, the same draft classes and the same generated players. Your best score of the week is kept in this browser; post your share card on Discord to compare.

- **Standard rules:** the scenario as written.
- **Short clock:** one season less than usual.
- **Tough GMs:** trades need tightly matched value.
- **Short clock, tough GMs:** both at once.

## Scoring and stars

- Every season scores 2 points per win plus a playoff bonus: 20 for the first round, 40 for the second, 70 for the conference finals, 120 for the Finals.
- A title scores 1,000 plus 250 for every season you had left.
- Stars: one for making the playoffs, two for reaching the Finals, three for winning it all.
- If you are fired, the challenge ends. Leagues where Sandbox or God Mode was used do not go on the board.

Your best score, stars and fastest title for each scenario show in the scenario picker and in the GM Locker.

## Strategy notes

- Short scenarios reward buying veterans early; long ones reward stacking picks and young players.
- Cap space is the fastest route to a star, but free agents weigh winning: a team with no hope rarely lands the best ones.
- Keep your owner happy: missing the season goals badly can cost you the job before the clock runs out.

---

# Real NBA history

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/real-nba-history.html

Real League starts from actual NBA history: pick any season from 1946-47 to today and take over a real team with its real roster, in a league that already holds every past season's stats, awards and champions.

## What is included

- Every player's year-by-year statistics, awards, All-Star selections and draft position up to your starting season.
- Rosters reconstructed from that season's real participation, with real jersey numbers.
- Real mid-season trades and the real draft classes of the coming years (optional).
- An option to load every real player, so players who retired before your start still have their careers and profiles.

## Ratings from statistics

Court Vision computes every player's ratings from his statistics: each season's players are ranked by production and given the Overall spread of a generated league, and skill attributes are estimated from his shooting, rebounding, passing and defensive numbers. The ratings are Court Vision's own; they are not official and not taken from any other game.

## Real Player Development

With Real Player Development on, real players follow their real careers: a rookie Jordan becomes the Jordan of 1991 on schedule, and players decline and retire when they really did. Players you create, draft from generated classes or import grow through Court Vision's own development. Turn it off to let every career go its own way.

## How ratings move over a career

A single season's rating can swing a lot. A star whose team adds another star, or a player who misses half a season, can drop 10 points or more on production alone. In Franchise leagues, where a player lives through many seasons, Court Vision smooths each career: every season is blended with the seasons either side, and a rating can move at most 6 points from one season to the next. A gap year, injury or comeback is not limited this way. Good players also get a small boost, up to +4 at the very top.

Single-season modes such as League Hunt and Career Mode cards keep the unsmoothed rating, because a card is one season.

## Real Player Development in detail

- It is on by default in historical leagues. At each season rollover, a real player's Overall moves to his reference rating for that real season.
- If he missed a real season (injury, or retiring and coming back), the gap is filled in a straight line between the seasons either side, and his profile labels it Interpolated.
- Before his first real season or after his last, there is nothing to follow. Court Vision's own aging, decline and retirement take over, and his profile says so. Nothing is extrapolated.
- Training, coaching, facilities and minutes still matter: they drive workload, recovery, morale and familiarity with systems and roles. They cannot permanently change a real player's base ratings while he follows his trajectory.

Players created, drafted from generated classes or imported grow through Court Vision's normal development. See [Coaching and player development](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/coaching-and-development.html).

## Drafts, debuts and the end of the data

- Each offseason, the real draft class for that year arrives as prospects with the usual scouting uncertainty.
- Players drafted earlier who debuted later (for example after playing overseas) join the team holding their rights in the season they really debuted.
- When your league runs past the last season in the data, draft classes become generated, fictional players, and the game tells you so.

## Real vs Yours

For every season your league has played that the data also covers, Real vs Yours compares the real champion, MVP and number 1 pick with your league's. The drift score is the share that came out differently: how far your timeline has moved from real history.

## Time Machine

Time Machine is a Franchise challenge that takes any real team-season, such as the 1996 Bulls, the 2016 Warriors or the 1967 76ers, and drops it into any other season. The travelling team plays with its real players exactly as they were that year. The rest of the league is real history from the season you land in. Your players become their own people in the new timeline, so "Michael Jordan '96" can meet the 1990 Michael Jordan, and they age and develop from there.

## Good starting points

- **1984-85:** the Jordan, Hakeem and Barkley rookie class.
- **1996-97:** Kobe, Iverson and Nash arrive; the Bulls are at their peak.
- **2003-04:** LeBron, Wade, Melo and Bosh enter the league.
- **2014-15:** the Warriors' first title season and the dawn of the three-point era.

---

# Ratings explained

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html

Court Vision uses a few different numbers. This page explains what each one means and how it is built.

## Player Overall

Overall is a weighted summary of a player's most important ratings for his position: shooting, finishing, playmaking, defense, rebounding and athleticism. It is a quick guide, not the whole story: the engine uses every individual rating and tendency, so two 75-rated players can play very differently.

## Team rating, 0 to 100

League Hunt rates teams from their best six players, weighted from the top (25%, 21%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 9%), because one great player is worth more than two good ones. That weighted strength is lined up against the real distribution of win totals across every team-season in NBA history, then turned into a rating:

| Rating | Real-world meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 60 | a bad team, about 25 wins |
| 70 | about 40 wins |
| 80 | about 45 wins |
| 90 | a 55 to 62 win team |
| 100 | a 68-win all-time great |

No real team goes past 100, but a squad built in League Hunt can.

## Ratings past 99

In Career Mode, the top 60 players ever at a skill carry ratings past 99, up to 120, ranked by what they really did: threes made (Stephen Curry), assists (John Stockton, Steve Nash), steals, rebounds and blocks (Wilt Chamberlain, Dikembe Mutombo). In games, every point past 99 counts half.

## Legacy Score

The Legacy Score measures a whole career. It is computed the same way for real players (from the NBA history data) and for players you create:

| Achievement | Points |
| --- | --- |
| MVP | 10 each |
| Finals MVP | 6 each |
| Championship | 5 each |
| All-NBA First / Second / Third Team | 5 / 3 / 1.5 each |
| Defensive Player of the Year | 3 each |
| All-Star selection | 1.5 each |
| All-Defensive First / Second Team | 1.2 / 0.6 each |
| Rookie of the Year | 1 |
| Career points / rebounds / assists | 1.6 / 0.9 / 1.2 per 1,000 |
| Career steals + blocks | 0.8 per 1,000 |

A Legacy Score of 45 puts a player in the Hall of Fame; 90 makes him a first-ballot pick.

## The all-time Top 100

The Top 100 is a fixed, hand-ordered list: LeBron James is 1, Michael Jordan 2, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar 3, Tim Duncan 4, Stephen Curry 7 and Kobe Bryant 12. A created player's place on it is one plus the number of listed players whose Legacy Score is higher than his.

---

# How the simulation works

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/how-the-simulation-works.html

Court Vision never invents a box score. Every game is played one possession at a time: someone gets the ball, makes a decision, and the play ends with a shot, a turnover or a foul. Points, rebounds and assists are counted from those events, so a player's statistics come from how he plays, not the other way round.

## One possession, step by step

Each trip down the floor runs through the same chain of decisions. Changing a player's ratings, tendencies or minutes changes what happens at each step, and the statistics follow.

1. **Who has the ball.** The engine picks a ball handler from the five players on the floor, weighted by each player's ball-handler priority. The weighting is steep rather than linear, so a true go-to star gets a much bigger share of touches than a role player, as usage concentrates on top options in real basketball. Priority is a setting you can edit, not something fixed by position.
2. **What he tries.** The possession becomes an action: an isolation, a pick-and-roll, a post-up, a drive, a catch-and-shoot look or a transition chance. Passing tendencies decide whether the ball moves; about a third of assisted shots come from a swing pass by someone other than the original ball handler.
3. **Does he keep the ball?** Before any shot, the engine checks for a turnover (see below).
4. **The shot.** If there is a shot, the engine chooses one of 14 shot types from the shooter's tendencies, rolls how well it is contested, and resolves the make or miss.
5. **Blocks, fouls and free throws.** A shot can be blocked, can draw a foul, or can be an and-one. Free throws are shot one at a time with the shooter's own free-throw ability.
6. **The rebound.** A miss goes to a rebounder chosen from all ten players.
7. **Fatigue.** Everyone on the floor gets a little more tired, and players on the bench recover.

## Fourteen shot types

A jump shot from the corner and a dunk are different skills, and Court Vision rates them separately. Each shot type reads the matching rating, so a great corner shooter is not automatically a great pull-up shooter.

| Group | Shot types |
| --- | --- |
| At the rim | Rim, close, layup, dunk |
| Mid-range | Mid-range, long mid-range, fadeaway, post shot, hook |
| Three-pointers | Corner three, above-the-break three, pull-up three, catch-and-shoot three, step-back |

Which type a player takes comes from his shot tendencies. You can edit them, or set a target number of three-point attempts, and the engine respects that instead of overriding it.

## Contests: open, light, contested, heavy

Every shot gets one of four contest levels. The defender's contest and closeout ratings push the roll toward tighter coverage. In the baseline tuning, roughly a quarter of shots are open.

The make chance depends on the shooter's ability for that shot type, the contest, his fatigue, and whether it is clutch time or the playoffs. Season shooting percentages are never used as an input: they are a result.

Fouls follow the contest too. A heavily contested shot draws a foul about three and a half times as often as an open one, and shots at the rim draw fouls far more often than threes. A disciplined defender fouls less.

## Turnovers are opportunities, not a position tax

A turnover is checked on each chance to lose the ball, using the ball handler's handle, ball security and decision making against the defender's perimeter defense and steal ratings, plus pressure from double teams and fatigue.

Because the model works per opportunity, an elite point guard turns the ball over less per touch than an average player. A point guard is not penalised just for having the ball more.

The engine tracks 13 kinds of turnover, including bad passes, steals in the passing lane, on-ball strips, charges, travels, double-team turnovers, shot-clock violations and illegal screens.

## Rebounds, blocks and height

- Rebounds compare offensive rebounding for the shooting team with defensive rebounding for the defense. Defenders get a positioning edge, tuned so the league-wide offensive rebound rate lands near the NBA's roughly 25%.
- Blocks use the defender's block and rim-protection ratings. Height past seven feet adds a little extra reach.
- Height matters, but it can never carry a player: it contributes at most about two points of Overall rating.

## Fatigue, minutes and injuries

- Fatigue builds every possession a player is on the floor, faster on hard possessions. Stamina and durability slow it down and speed up recovery on the bench. A tired player's ratings are multiplied down, so a gassed star really does shoot worse.
- Each player's minutes can be left to the AI, given a target, set exactly, or planned by hand. The substitution planner works toward those totals over the game.
- Injuries are rolled per possession but kept rare, tuned so a full 82-game season gives each team a plausible handful, not one every game. Some quick modes, such as Survival, play with injuries off.

## Badges and ratings above 99

Badges change ratings or switch on special rules, and the engine reads them all the same way, without a special case for each badge. See the [badges guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/badges-explained.html) for the full list.

Some modes let ratings go past 99. On the court, every point above 99 counts half, so a 120 shooter is the best ever but not automatic.

## Same seed, same game

Every game is driven by a seeded random number generator. The same seed and the same rosters and settings replay the same game, possession for possession. This is how the shared daily and weekly challenges give everyone the same games, and how a saved game can be replayed on the court exactly as it happened.

## Make it your own

League settings expose many of these dials: shooting variance, turnover and foul frequency, era rules such as the three-point line, injuries and more. Sandbox mode unlocks experimental badges and editing for testing ideas. New to the game? Start with [How to Play](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html).

---

# Badges explained

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/badges-explained.html

Badges are small, specific boosts on top of a player's ratings. A Deep Range shooter really gets more out of his above-the-break threes; a Lockdown defender really contests harder. Court Vision has 27 normal badges that players can earn and 17 experimental badges for the Sandbox.

## How badges work

- A normal badge adds points to particular ratings. The bonus applies on top of the player's base ratings when he plays; his base ratings are never changed, so taking a badge away restores him exactly.
- Badges do not stack: each one counts once.
- The engine reads every badge the same way, so a badge does exactly what its description says and nothing hidden.

## Shooting badges

| Badge | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Deep Range | +6 three-point, +5 above-the-break threes |
| Deadeye | +7 shot IQ, +3 offensive consistency |
| Quick Release | +5 catch-and-shoot, +5 offensive IQ |
| Catch & Shoot | +8 catch-and-shoot, +4 corner threes |
| Difficult Shots | +6 mid-range, +5 post fade, +3 shot IQ |
| Pull-Up Specialist | +8 pull-up threes, +4 long mid-range |

## Ball-handling badges

| Badge | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Handles | +7 ball handling, +3 speed with the ball |
| Unpluckable | +8 ball security |
| Tight Handle | +4 ball handling, +5 decision making |
| Speed Booster | +7 speed with the ball, +3 acceleration |

These matter more than they look. Turnovers are checked on each chance to lose the ball, so better handling and security cut a guard's turnovers directly. See [How the simulation works](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/how-the-simulation-works.html).

## Defense badges

| Badge | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Rim Protector | +6 rim protection, +5 block |
| Lockdown | +7 perimeter defense, +4 contest |
| Interceptor | +7 passing-lane steal, +4 steal IQ |
| Pick Pocket | +7 on-ball steal, +4 steal |
| Chase Down | +6 block timing, +3 speed, +3 vertical |
| Glass Cleaner | +7 defensive rebounding, +5 offensive rebounding |

## Finishing and passing badges

| Badge | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Contact Finisher | +6 finishing, +4 strength |
| Acrobat | +7 driving layup, +4 touch |
| Posterizer | +7 driving dunk, +4 vertical |
| Dimer | +6 passing IQ, +4 passing |
| Needle Threader | +7 passing accuracy, +3 passing |
| Bail Out | +6 decision making, +4 passing accuracy |

Five more round out the list: Post Craft, Corner Specialist, Iron Man, Switchable and Floor General. Each player's profile shows exactly what his badges add.

## Earning badges

In a league with player development turned on, a player earns a normal badge by having enough of the underlying ability, backing it up with sustained, efficient play in real games, and practising the right skill. Progress moves through broad stages and can slip back if he stops producing. A player cannot be given a badge just for playing a lot of minutes.

For more on practice plans and coaches, read [Coaching and player development](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/coaching-and-development.html).

## Experimental badges (Sandbox only)

Experimental badges break the rules on purpose, for testing and for fun. They are only available in Sandbox mode, along with manual badge editing, so they never sneak into a normal league.

- **Perfect Shooter**, **Perfect Blocker** and **Perfect Steal**: eligible attempts always succeed.
- **Never Turnover**: the player cannot lose the ball.
- **Infinite Stamina**: fatigue never builds.
- **Unlimited Range**: distance stops hurting his shot.
- Also: God Speed, Clutch God, Playoff God, No Injury, No Foul, Automatic Assist, Rebound God, Gravity, Unblockable Shot, Unstealable Ball and Infinite Vertical.

Try one on a single player and watch a few games: it is a fast way to see how much one skill moves a team's results.

---

# Survival guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/survival.html

Survival: Last Team Standing starts you with a stacked team of all-time greats. You play real teams from NBA history one game at a time, each under its own era's rules. Every win has a price: the team you beat claims one of your players. One loss and the run is over.

## Build the team

1. You are dealt 14 great players from all of history, one season each: five guards, five forwards and four centers. At least one legendary season comes at each position; the rest are epic.
2. Keep ten of them. That is your whole roster.
3. Name a **Franchise Player**. He can never be claimed, whatever happens.

## Each round

- You see the next opponent and its rating before tip-off. Opponents are real historical teams, and you never face the same team twice in a run.
- The game is played under the opponent's era rules, with its era's coaching style.
- Lose and the run ends. Win and the beaten team claims one of your players (never the Franchise Player). Then you sign one of three of their players to refill your roster.
- Every fifth round is a **boss** game against a champion team.

## Shields

You start with one Shield, and each boss win adds another, up to three. When a team claims a player you want to keep, spend a Shield: the claim is blocked and they take someone else instead. You can only shield once a round.

## Cash and emergency signings

Each win pays 25 cash, and a boss win pays 50. Before a round you can spend 60 on one emergency signing from three free agents, players a little below your team's average who are not already on your roster. It fills an empty spot or replaces your lowest-rated player, never the Franchise Player. One emergency signing per round.

## Three levels

| Level | Opponents | Who they claim | Score multiplier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rookie | Softer | One of your top four, not always the best | 0.75x |
| Pro | Standard climb | One of your two best | 1x |
| Legend | Tougher from the start | Always your best | 1.5x |

On every level the opposition gets steadily stronger: each round adds a little to every opposing player, so late rounds stay dangerous.

## Scoring

Your score is 100 points per win, 150 more for each boss beaten, and 2 points per point of winning margin (up to 25 a game), all multiplied by the level. Your run is shared as a strip of squares, a crown for each boss.

The **Daily Survival** deals the same legends, opponents and games to everyone for the same choices, so you can compare runs with friends. Relics do not apply in the Daily.

## Strategy

- Pick a Franchise Player you can build around for many rounds, usually the best two-way star rather than the highest Overall.
- Depth wins long runs: your team rating counts your best eight, starters most. A tenth man rarely matters; a sixth man often does.
- Save Shields for your second-best player, since the best one is often the Franchise Player and already safe.
- When you sign from a beaten team, refill the position you just lost.
- Learn how team ratings are built in [Ratings explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html).

---

# Your Career guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/your-career.html

Your Career follows one player from a youth club at 13 to his last game. You build him, then every season brings choices: which school, stay or transfer, when to declare for the draft, which contract, how to train. The seasons in between play themselves.

## Create your player

- Choose a name, number, country, position and height. Each position has its own height range and weighs ratings differently in your Overall: point guards lean on vision and handles, centers on physical play and defense.
- Pick a background. **City courts** start with more reputation and handles; a **small town** player starts unknown with more room to grow; a **hoops family** brings good habits and a famous name to live up to.
- Answer eight playing-style questions, from how you like to score to what your summer workouts look like. Each answer moves your starting ratings, and leaning hard one way costs you a little elsewhere.
- Your five ratings are shooting, dribbling, vision, defense and physical. Your strongest two give you an archetype, such as Floor General, Slasher or Rim Protector.

## The road to the pros

| Level | Ages | Games a season |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Youth club | 13-14 | 30 |
| High school | 14-17 | 28 |
| College or pro academy | 18+ | 34 (college), 36 (academy) |
| Europe | 18+ | 34 |
| G League | Pro | 48 |
| NBA | Pro | 82 |

Each level is tougher than the last, so a player who dominated in high school can find college much harder. After high school, recruiting offers decide where you go next.

## Declaring for the draft

At the end of each college year you can declare, come back for another year, enter the transfer portal, or test the waters and keep your eligibility. Scouts give a projection from Top 3 pick down to likely undrafted. It depends mostly on your Overall, then your reputation and your age, because teams pay for upside. After four college years, or out of an academy, you must go pro.

## Contracts and free agency

When a contract runs out, the phone rings. NBA players can re-sign with a loyalty bonus. Other offers come in three kinds: a **contender** with title odds but maybe a bench role, a rebuilding team offering **max money** on a shorter deal, or a team that wants you to be **the guy**. From age 33 you can also retire.

## Growth and aging

Young players improve fastest: about three and a half points a season in the early teens, slowing through the early twenties, and nearly flat by 28. From 30, ratings start to fall, faster every year. Each season you choose a training focus, and between seasons story events ask you to decide what to do when things go right or wrong.

Your career ends when you retire, at 41 at the latest, or earlier if your Overall falls too low after 35.

## Awards and Legacy

- Every level has its own trophies: youth national titles, State champion and All-State, college honors, and in the NBA Rookie of the Year, All-Star, All-NBA, MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, Sixth Man of the Year, championships and Finals MVP.
- Your **Legacy** score counts NBA seasons only: how far your Overall rose above 70, your scoring, and your trophies, with an MVP worth the most.
- A Legacy of 160 or more puts you in the Hall of Fame.

## Tips

- Pick a position that fits your height range: a 6-foot center is a long road.
- Staying in college another year can raise your draft stock, but the projection rewards youth, so do not wait too long.
- For an all-time career in the classic GM game, try [Career Mode](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/career-mode.html) instead.

---

# Story Mode guide

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/story-mode.html

Story Mode: Street to the League follows one player from a park in his hometown to the NBA. Scenes ask you to choose who you trust, how you train and what you say. Key games are played by the main game engine with you on the floor, and how you play changes the story.

## Choose your style

| Style | Position | Plays like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bucket getter | Shooting guard | Three levels, no conscience: born to score |
| Floor general | Point guard | Sees the play before it happens |
| Two-way wing | Small forward | Locks up their best, knocks down the open three |
| Paint beast | Center | Rebounds, blocks, dunks |

You also pick a hometown, from Baltimore to Oakland, Chicago's South Side to New Orleans.

## The five chapters

1. **The Blacktop** (age 16): summer at Carver Park, and a run against the city's top sophomore.
2. **Varsity** (17): tryouts, the season opener, a rivalry game, and a shot at the state title.
3. **The Circuit** (18): AAU summer, a showcase in Las Vegas, recruiting rankings, and people who want something from you.
4. **The Choice** (19): where you play next.
5. **Draft Night** (20): the moment everything has been building to.

After the draft, the story continues for fifteen seasons in the real NBA.

## The people on the road

Four people walk the road with you: your best friend Dre, Coach Ray from the rec center, your little sister Maya, and your rival Marcus "Ice" Vance. Choices build or strain each relationship. On one Friday night you can go to a party with Dre (more hype, a closer friendship), work out with Coach Ray (better playmaking and more grit, but Dre feels left out), stay in and watch film, or take Maya to the movies as you promised.

## Games and training

- Key games are real simulations with you on the floor. A win or a loss changes the next scene, your hype and your options.
- Training sessions give you points to spend on your skills before the next stretch of games.
- Your choices and results raise or lower your hype and grit, which shape what comes next.

## Endings

The ending depends on your career, your hype, your grit and the people you kept close. Everything is seeded, so the same choices tell the same story. Make different ones to see where else the road goes.

## Related modes

Want more control over a whole career? [Your Career](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/your-career.html) starts at 13 with more choices about schools and contracts, and [Career Mode](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/career-mode.html) builds a player for the full GM game.

---

# Coaching and player development

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/coaching-and-development.html

In a franchise league you run the coaching staff as well as the roster. Coaches, systems, rotations and practice all feed the possession engine and how players grow, rather than adding a flat bonus to a rating.

## Your staff

- Five jobs: head coach, offensive assistant, defensive assistant, development coach and athletic trainer.
- Each coach has ten separate coaching ratings, specialties, preferences, a personality and a career record.
- Hire through the **Staff Market**. Candidates weigh salary, contract length, role, how good your team is, your facilities and fit, and interviews explain what they care about.
- Firing a coach pays out his contract and brings a short adjustment period. Assistants can be promoted, and successful development coaches may leave to become head coaches.

## Systems and schemes

Pick one of six offensive systems and one of five defensive schemes. Each fits some rosters better than others, and players get more familiar with it over time. The trade-offs are basketball ones: motion offense creates more assisted shots, isolation concentrates usage, drop coverage gives up perimeter looks, and pressure defense has its weaknesses.

## Rotations

Choose a rotation style (fixed, performance, development, matchup or playoff), then set preferred starters and closing, small-ball and defensive groups, plus a backup ball handler. You can still lock exact or manual minutes for any player, and the engine will respect them. See [How the simulation works](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/how-the-simulation-works.html) for how minutes and fatigue interact.

## Practice and development plans

- A seven-day practice calendar covers skills, offense, defense, conditioning, film and recovery. Auto Practice plans around the schedule, fatigue and the playoffs. Injured players train on restrictions.
- Each player can get a primary and secondary focus, an intensity, a target role, an assigned coach and a veteran mentor.
- Growth is skill by skill and never certain. It depends on age, work ethic, teaching, how high a rating already is, health, playing time and your league's development settings. Piling on minutes is not the best way to develop a young player, and potential is not a guarantee.
- Long-term projects track progress and stalls over months. Cancel one and the gains he already made stay.

## Mentors, morale and badges

- A mentor must be at least 27 and four years older than his mentee, and can take two mentees at most. Mentoring supports the right training and relationships; it does not copy ratings or badges.
- Role conversations affect trust and morale, and can come with a ten-game promise about minutes. Break the promise and there are consequences; repeating the conversation does not farm morale.
- Players earn normal badges through ability, efficient play and practice. See [Badges explained](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/badges-explained.html).

## How much control you want

| Setting | Staff | Plans | Practice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Simple | Automatic | Automatic | Automatic |
| Standard | Manual | Manual | Automatic |
| Deep | Manual | Manual | Manual |

AI teams use the same systems: they hire, train, mentor and change rotations, protect older players from heavy minutes, and can replace an underperforming coach when a better one is affordable. New to franchise play? Start with [How to Play](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html).

---

# Frequently asked questions

URL: https://courtvisiongame.com/faq.html

Choose a topic or search for a question. These answers explain the game available now, from your first franchise to protecting a long-running save. For a step-by-step franchise walkthrough, read [How to Play](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html).

## What is CourtVision?

CourtVision is a basketball management and simulation game by NineFoldVision. You make roster, training and coaching decisions, then the simulation plays out possessions and produces results. You can run a franchise, build historical teams for short challenges, or follow one player through a career. Pixel-art games let you watch the action as well as read the statistics.

## Is Court Vision free?

Yes. Court Vision is free to play, with no purchases. The web version is supported by advertising. Ad availability depends on your settings, connection and whether an ad is served, and the offline Windows edition shows no ads.

## How do I start playing?

Open the game and choose a mode on the main menu. Choose **Franchise** for a league you manage over multiple seasons; its setup includes real historical leagues, generated leagues and challenges. Choose **82-0 Challenge** for a focused team-building run, or **Career Mode** to follow one player. Read the setup rules before starting: each mode has its own goals and options.

For your first franchise, pick a team, inspect its roster, set a rotation and simulate a game before advancing a whole season. The [beginner guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html) walks through trades, the schedule and the offseason.

## Do I need an account?

No account is required for local single-player play. An optional account enables cloud progress and online features: leaderboards, a public profile, PvP, clubs and clans, friend gifts and Online Leagues. You must be 13 or older to create an account. Online features require an internet connection and an available account service; they are not the same as local saves.

## Can I play on my phone?

The game includes mobile layouts and runs in modern phone browsers. Large roster tables may need horizontal scrolling, and longer simulations can take more time on a phone. Try a short challenge first, keep the tab open while it runs, and use a larger screen when you want more room for detailed management.

If Google sign-in fails inside Instagram or another in-app browser, open CourtVision in your normal browser and start sign-in there.

## Is downloading required?

No. The browser version starts from the website. Installation is optional: the [installation guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/./#/install) explains adding the app to supported devices. A Windows download is also linked there. Your browser and the installed edition may keep separate local saves, so use a backup when moving between them.

## What game modes are there, and how long do they take?

The seven main menu choices are **Franchise, League Hunt, 82-0 Challenge, Career Mode, Survival, Story Mode and Your Career**. Franchise includes additional setups such as Rebuild Challenge and All-Time Draft. Some modes offer daily, weekly or difficulty variants.

Short challenges can fit a brief session, while franchise management can continue for many seasons. Actual time depends on your device, how much you watch and how many decisions you make; menu time estimates are not limits.

## How does Franchise Mode work?

Manage a team across the season and offseason: set rotations, hire staff, trade, negotiate contracts, scout prospects and draft. Real historical setups and generated leagues offer different starting points. Budgets, roster needs and player development make a strong team a longer-term project than simply collecting high overall ratings.

The Franchise setup also includes Rebuild Challenge, All-Time Draft, Time Machine and World Games options. Check each setup for its rules. Start with [How to Play](https://courtvisiongame.com/how-to-play.html), then use the [guides](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/) for a particular challenge.

## How does Hunt Mode work?

In **League Hunt**, spin a six-player squad and a coach, lock your choices, and choose a training focus. The standard road contains ten best-of-seven series under historical era rules, with a semi-boss and a final boss. Between series you choose boosts and visit shops at designated stops.

Losing a series costs a life; the starting number depends on difficulty. Spend resources with the next matchup in mind, rather than only raising one star’s rating. Special variants and bonus opponents can change the run. See the [League Hunt guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/league-hunt.html).

## What is the 82-0 Challenge?

Build a ten-player team and choose a coach, then try to win all 82 regular-season games and go 16-0 in the playoffs. Setup choices include quick spins, franchise-and-era selections and category-based drafting. A team of scorers still needs defense, rebounding and a workable rotation.

Daily and other variants have their own setup rules. Results and records let you compare runs even when you fall short of perfection. Read the [82-0 guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/82-0-challenge.html).

## How does Career Mode work?

Create a player through the historical-player wheel or the MyPlayer builder, then follow his seasons, training, team changes, awards and retirement. Wheel choices combine different aspects of real players into your created player; they do not copy one historical career exactly.

Career Mode summarizes a whole playing career and evaluates its legacy. It is separate from **Your Career**, which starts younger and focuses on season-by-season life and basketball choices. See the [Career Mode guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/career-mode.html).

## How does Your Career Mode work?

Start a player at age 13 and choose his identity, position and playing style. Decisions shape training and the route through youth basketball, school, college and professional opportunities. Later choices include entering the draft and selecting contracts.

Read the options each season: this mode is about shaping a path over time, rather than using the Career Mode wheel to assemble a finished starting build.

## How does Survival Mode work?

Choose ten players from the opening deal and designate a Franchise Player who cannot be taken. Play historical opponents one game at a time. After a win, the opponent can claim one of your strongest players and you choose a replacement from its offers. Difficulty changes which players are at risk.

Shields protect against player claims; they do not normally erase a lost game. A loss ends the run. Boss opponents appear every fifth round, so saving a shield and maintaining a balanced rotation matter. The Daily Survival uses a shared seed and disables relic bonuses.

## How does Story Mode work?

**Street to the League** follows a basketball story from the park toward a professional career. Story cards, relationships and decisions connect the games, with different endings depending on the path you take. Games use the simulation engine, while the story gives those results a narrative setting.

Choose Story Mode when you want characters and choices alongside basketball, rather than full control of an entire franchise.

## How do player ratings and attributes work?

Overall is a summary, not a guarantee of performance. Individual shooting, finishing, passing, defense, rebounding and physical attributes describe different skills. Tendencies influence what a player attempts, while roles, minutes, teammates and opponents affect the opportunities he gets.

Compare attributes relevant to your lineup: a shooter needs spacing and touches; a defensive big can help without leading the scoring. Rating scales and caps differ between modes and special options. The [ratings guide](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/ratings-explained.html) explains the main summaries.

## How do historical basketball eras work?

Historical franchise setups start with teams and players from the selected season. Era settings and historical challenge matchups can change rules and styles, including three-point availability, pace and defensive conditions. A modern shooting lineup therefore does not play every historical matchup under today’s conditions.

Historical statistics supply inputs, but CourtVision’s ratings and simulated outcomes are its own model. A replay is not a promise to reproduce real standings or careers. Read [Real NBA history](https://courtvisiongame.com/guides/real-nba-history.html).

## How do draft classes and scouting work?

Franchise drafts let you compare prospects and use scouting information before making a selection. Historical and generated setups provide different prospect pools. Scout estimates of potential are not certain forecasts: current ability, development and your team’s needs all matter.

Inspect the available reports and player details, compare prospects at the positions you need, and keep more than one target in mind before your pick. The highest estimated potential is not automatically the best immediate starter.

## How do players develop?

Players change over seasons rather than remaining fixed at their starting rating. Age, potential and development systems affect their progression; training choices let you emphasize aspects of a player’s game. Historical development settings can also influence how real players progress.

Use the player’s current skills and role when choosing training. A promising prospect still needs time, and an older star may decline. The outcome is a simulation, not a guaranteed growth schedule.

## Can I watch games and coach?

Yes. The game supports simulated results and a pixel-art Watch Game view. Coaching controls include rotations and tactical decisions; the available controls depend on the mode and screen. Team construction and coaching influence the simulation, but do not guarantee the result of an individual possession.

For franchise management, review the box score as well as the result. Shooting efficiency, turnovers, rebounds and playing time can help explain why a higher-rated roster lost.

## What is Sandbox mode?

Sandbox provides editing tools for experimenting with a league, including player editing and importing historical players. It changes the competitive context: leagues marked as using Sandbox do not qualify for the normal GM achievement and Rebuild Challenge checks. Keep a separate save if you want both an experiment and a competitive franchise.

## How do relics and rarity work?

The Relic Vault contains Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythic relics, plus Secret relics with special abilities. Regular relics contribute luck when equipped in available slots. Duplicate rewards, stacking, upgrades and extra slots are handled by the Vault; simply owning every relic does not equip them all.

Earned rewards and coins can supply more spins. Read the Vault’s current descriptions and odds before spending coins. Shared daily and weekly challenges can disable luck and special abilities to keep their starting conditions comparable.

## What are Lucky Spins?

In the Relic Vault, Lucky Spins use a different rarity distribution and exclude Common relics. They can use earned Lucky Spins or the displayed coin price. They improve the distribution; they do not make every result a Mythic or Secret.

The Career wheel also uses the phrase Lucky Spin for its own player-building mechanic. Follow the explanation on the screen you are using: a Vault spin rewards a relic, while a Career wheel choice affects your player build.

## What is my GM level?

Your profile accumulates XP from supported completed activities and achievements across modes. Level and achievement rewards include progression and cosmetic unlocks, which you can inspect in the profile and GM Locker. The game checks eligibility, so not every edited or experimental result earns competitive progress.

## What is the Mode of the Week?

The menu highlights a featured mode that earns bonus XP. Check the current featured-mode panel before starting a run, because the selection rotates and reward limits apply. Daily goals and achievements offer other objectives when you want something more specific than another season.

## How do leaderboards work?

Community boards compare supported results, profile progression and other records. Sign in to associate online submissions with your account. Different boards measure different things: XP, a career legacy score and a challenge result are not interchangeable rankings.

Shared challenges use their own seeds and eligibility rules. A result must sync successfully before it can appear online; a local record alone does not prove that the server received it.

## Where are my saves? Can I lose them?

Leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds are stored locally in the browser, using browser databases and local storage. Clearing site data, using private browsing, changing browser profiles or switching devices can make those saves unavailable.

An account syncs supported profile progress and retired Career Mode records, not a full copy of every league. Use **Backup everything** in Backups or the GM Locker to download a separate file. A successful cloud sync is not a replacement for a league backup.

Online Leagues are an explicit exception: they share league snapshots through the server. Your Career also syncs its player progress with an account. These features do not turn every local franchise save into a cloud backup.

## How do I move my progress to another device?

Download **Backup everything** on the original device. Open CourtVision on the destination device and choose **Restore from a file**. Read the confirmation before restoring: matching records can be replaced, while other records remain. Back up the destination device first if it has progress you want to preserve.

Account sign-in can bring supported synced progress across devices, but active leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds require a backup. Authentication sessions and account passes are not transferred as ordinary backup data.

## What should I do if the game crashes?

First reopen CourtVision in the same browser and profile, then check your saved games. Do not clear site data as a first troubleshooting step: that can delete the local save you are trying to recover. A crash before a save completes may lose recent actions.

For a franchise, check the save recovery controls for available restore points. **Restore as New League** opens a separate recovered save. A downloaded backup is another option. Recovery is only possible if a usable save, restore point or backup exists.

## Why does a simulated season take a few seconds?

A season involves many games, each with possessions and player statistics, plus league updates and offseason work. Larger leagues and longer careers require more calculation. The game uses background workers for simulation jobs, but device speed, memory and browser limits still affect completion time.

Keep the tab open while a job runs and avoid repeatedly starting the same action. If it appears stuck, note the mode, season, action and any error message before reopening the game or reporting it.

## Can I play offline?

The installed web app can reuse cached files, and the Windows edition is designed for offline play. Open the modes you need while connected first; cached data can be missing or cleared, so offline availability is not guaranteed for every first-time action.

Signing in, cloud sync, online boards and other server-backed features need a connection. Keep a local backup before relying on offline play or switching editions.

## I found a bug or have an idea

Use the [Contact and support page](https://courtvisiongame.com/contact.html): post in the Discord community or email [papashvilisaba4@gmail.com](mailto:papashvilisaba4@gmail.com). Include your mode, browser, device, what you expected, what happened and the steps that trigger it. A screenshot of an error can help.

Do not post passwords, sign-in links or account tokens. Backup files contain your game data; share one only when needed for diagnosis and after checking what it includes. For recovery steps, see the crash and saving answers above.

## How do accounts work?

The web game supports optional Google or Discord sign-in through Supabase Auth. CourtVision uses the provider’s sign-in flow instead of asking you to create a separate game password. A session is kept in your browser so you can stay signed in.

Choose your GM name and check the account’s sync status when moving between devices. On a shared computer, take care which account is signed in: switching accounts can replace the local set of synced profile progress with the other account’s progress.

## Is there an age requirement?

Anyone can play locally without an account. To create an account you must be 13 or older, and you confirm this before signing in. Accounts unlock public features such as GM names, profiles, leaderboards, clubs and clans. See the [Terms of Use](https://courtvisiongame.com/terms.html) and the [Privacy Policy](https://courtvisiongame.com/privacy.html).

## What information is stored with my account?

The account system uses an account identifier, email and provider details, a GM profile, and supported game progress. Public profiles and boards display information such as your GM name, level, statistics and submitted results. Retired created players can also be public.

Local league saves are separate from cloud profile progress. Optional online features such as Online Leagues, clubs, clans and friend gifts store additional records. Read the [Privacy Policy](https://courtvisiongame.com/privacy.html) for the current disclosures, and avoid putting private information in your public GM name.

If you deliberately create or join an Online League, its shared league state is uploaded to Supabase storage so other members can play it. That is separate from ordinary single-player franchise saves. Your Career also includes account-synced player progress; this differs from an in-progress Career Mode world.

## Can I delete my account or request help with my data?

The account screen in Community includes account deletion. It calls the server to delete the account; wait for confirmation rather than assuming a failed request worked. Local progress is separate and is not erased just by deleting the account.

For a privacy request or a deletion problem, email [papashvilisaba4@gmail.com](mailto:papashvilisaba4@gmail.com). See [Contact and support](https://courtvisiongame.com/contact.html).

## How are cookies and browser storage used?

The game uses local storage and browser databases for saves, settings and account-related state. Google advertising can use cookies or similar technologies. The web version also integrates host analytics and Umami for usage measurements; these are distinct from saving a league.

Open **Cookie Settings** in the game to revisit the configured advertising consent options. Existing third-party cookies may need to be removed using browser controls. Clearing all site data also removes local game progress, so download a backup first. See the [Privacy Policy](https://courtvisiongame.com/privacy.html).

## Does CourtVision display advertisements?

The web version is configured for Google AdSense banner placements. Whether an ad appears depends on consent handling, ad availability, connection and blockers. Advertising does not need to load for local gameplay to work. The offline Windows build excludes network ads.

Google’s regional consent message is managed through the site’s advertising configuration. Read the [Privacy Policy](https://courtvisiongame.com/privacy.html) and use the game’s Cookie Settings for your available choices.

## Is Court Vision affiliated with the NBA?

No. CourtVision is an independent game by NineFoldVision, not an official NBA product and not endorsed by the NBA, its teams or players. The [About page](https://courtvisiongame.com/about.html) identifies the historical data sources and distinguishes those statistics from the game’s own ratings and simulation.

## Can I play the same league as a friend?

A league code lets a friend start from the same league setup while playing a separate simulation. Online Leagues are a different feature: signed-in members share a league state through the server. Check the relevant setup and account status before choosing between a parallel challenge and a shared league.

## How do ranked seasons and PvP work?

Ranked competition and League Hunt PvP are available through the online community features. Ranked events contribute points under their own rules; Hunt PvP uses a submitted squad against other players’ teams and tracks a rating. These features require account services and differ from a local single-player run. Check the current event and submission screens for eligibility and results.
